expected.full: Shoot it as a professional architectural interior photograph: full-frame camera, 24–35 mm rectilinear lens at eye level about 1.5 m, f/8 with everything in focus, vertical lines kept perfectly vertical, no fisheye. Lighting: bright natural daylight on an overcast-to-sunny morning, neutral white balance around 5000K, soft large-source light with gentle falloff across the room; warm LED strip light under the wall cabinets washes the backsplash and countertop (subtle in daylight). Materials: wood surfaces show natural, non-repeating grain running consistently along each panel, with true-to-scale grain size and subtle variation between boards; laminate and melamine panels have a fine low-sheen texture with soft, broad reflections; matte painted fronts have an even satin finish with no plastic shine; the stone countertop has a crisp eased edge, realistic veining that continues across the front edge, and a light polished reflection of the wall cabinets; metal handles and appliances show brushed metal with directional micro-scratches and soft specular highlights; tiles have thin recessed grout lines and slightly varying glaze reflections. Physically plausible detail: thin dark shadow lines in the 2–3 mm reveal gaps between doors and drawers; soft ambient-occlusion contact shadows where cabinets meet the wall, floor and ceiling, and in inside corners; a soft shadow under the countertop overhang and inside the toe-kick recess; door and panel edges have tiny rounded bevels that catch a thin line of light; a soft shadow band on the backsplash under the wall cabinets. Natural color, realistic dynamic range (no HDR look), very fine natural sensor grain, accurate white balance; the room looks clean and newly installed, with no people, text or clutter. It must be indistinguishable from a real photograph, not a 3D render.
